raw.title: Platform Security Engineer
raw.description:
At Scality, we build software that stores and protects the world’s most critical data — running on Linux, inside some of the largest infrastructures on the planet, at exabyte scale, for organizations that cannot afford to fail.

We are looking for a Platform Security Engineer to join our platform and delivery team in Paris. This is a new seat, and it exists because security work needs dedicated capacity. Absorbed as background tasks between feature tickets, it never gets the focus it deserves. You would be that dedicated capacity.

This is a Linux-first, hands-on engineering role. You will not write policies for other people to implement — you will write the Python and Bash that hardens our OS, automates our vulnerability management, and proves to auditors and customers that our supply chain is sound.


About Scality

Scality is the leader in software-defined object storage, trusted by 1,000+ enterprises and 700M+ users worldwide across banking, healthcare, and government sectors — exactly the sectors where security posture is a purchasing criterion, not a checkbox.

Industry recognition:

  • Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for 9 consecutive years — the only 100% software-defined storage company to hold this position since the quadrant’s inception
  • #1 on the GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Object Storage (2024), ahead of 17 competing vendors
  • Gold Stevie Award 2025 — ARTESCA 3.0, Cloud Storage & Backup Solution category
  • Net Promoter Score of 85 across RING and ARTESCA

About the team

You will join a small team of highly skilled Linux engineers responsible for delivering and maintaining ADI (Scality Autonomous Data Infrastructure), our full platform: RING (object storage), S3C (S3-compatible layer), and SCOS (Scality OS — our own Linux distribution).

The team works across the full stack of infrastructure engineering — deep Linux system integration, RPM packaging, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and release automation. The command line is where most of our day happens, and we ship a Linux distribution to customers.


How We Build

We build with AI tools, in earnest rather than as an experiment. Every engineer here has Claude Code, and it is part of how we write, review, and ship code day to day.

We are also designing something larger: an AI code and delivery factory — AI woven into the build and release chain itself, not just into the editor. That work is early and still being thought through rather than already solved. We expect it to become part of how we maintain the platform, and CVE remediation is one of the first places we think it fits: an automated path from advisory to assessment to a patched, tested, delivered build.

If that sounds like a problem you would want to work on, this role sits close to it.

One principle is not negotiable: a human owns the outcome. AI writes code here, and when it does, we own what it produces — the review, the decision to ship, the consequences, and the fix. “The tool did it” is not an explanation we accept from ourselves, and it is not one we would offer a customer. In security work that matters doubly: an answer you cannot defend is worse than no answer at all.


How This Role Works

Scality is building a network of security engineers across the engineering department — a security peer embedded in each development team, rather than a central security function working at arm’s length from the code. You would be that peer for the platform and delivery team.

  • Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering. The agenda is set at that level, with dedicated resources committed across the teams. You will not have to invent it alone — and you will have a voice in it: the engineers closest to the code help decide what goes on the roadmap. We will be straight with you: today security work competes with delivery commitments and too often loses. Naming an owner and funding dedicated people is how we intend to change that. You would help build that capability, not inherit a finished one.
  • The team is accountable for the deliveries. Security items sit on the team’s plate alongside everything else it commits to, rather than in a separate function filing tickets from the outside.
  • You are the dedicated resource that makes them happen. While your teammates carry releases, OS compatibility, and platform features, your time is reserved for the security work. That focus is the whole reason the seat exists.
  • You share the team’s perimeter and its knowledge. Same repositories, same Jira projects, same code reviews, same sprint rituals. The engineers around you have rare, hard-earned Linux depth — OS integration, RPM packaging, boot and GRUB, CI/CD, monitoring — and you will learn the platform from them.
  • You will have peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams work the same problems on different perimeters. That network is where you compare notes, share tooling, and grow into the craft.

    • The point of the model is that security decisions get made inside the team that builds and ships the product, by someone who understands the build system rather than filing tickets against it.


Your First Missions

Two priorities are already on the roadmap, and they will shape your first year.

1. CVE exposure, answered before it is asked

Customers in banking, healthcare, and government ask us, routinely and under their own audit obligations, whether our products are exposed to a given CVE. That will not stop — for them, asking is the compliance requirement. Today each answer is researched from scratch: a customer question becomes a ticket, the ticket becomes a hunt through SBOMs, vendor advisories, and our own configuration, and the round trip can take weeks to produce something the team is not fully confident defending.

Your first mission is to invert that, so the answer already exists when the question arrives.

  • A standing exposure record, per shipped component and per release: what the SBOM says is present, what the upstream vendor has decided (including “will not fix”, which is common on RHEL 8 and often the real answer), and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in our configuration
  • Reachability over presence. A module shipped and loaded by a distribution default is not the same as a module configured on a live URL. That distinction is the difference between “vulnerable” and “no impact”, and it is where the engineering judgement lives
  • Continuous CVE detection across our repositories, vendored third-party modules, container images, and shipped RPMs
  • Wiring detection into our existing SBOM tooling and GitHub Actions pipelines, so exposure is computed when a release is built rather than when a customer asks
  • A defined interface with the security engineers and the customer-facing teams: who produces the technical assessment, who owns the wording that reaches the customer, and how both meet the response commitments in our customer security policy
  • Durable capture. An assessment that lives only in a ticket comment gets re-derived next release. Findings belong somewhere queryable
  • A remediation loop with clear ownership and response targets, integrated with how the team already works in Jira
  • AI-assisted remediation, where it fits: from advisory to proposed patch to a tested build, with a human deciding what ships

    • Done well, a customer’s “are you affected by X?” becomes a lookup and an afternoon, not an escalation and three weeks.

    2. Raising the security baseline of SCOS

    SCOS is our own Linux distribution — we control the kickstarts, the package set, the boot path, and the images. That is unusual leverage, and we intend to use it. You will drive platform-level hardening across the OS we ship:

    • A hardened, defensible default configuration for the distribution
    • Advancing SELinux enforcement across RING and S3C (work already begun on the team, which you will help carry)
    • Supply-chain integrity: artifact provenance, signing, dependency currency, reproducible and verifiable builds
    • Secrets and credential handling across the delivery pipeline
    • Cryptographic posture — including FIPS 140-3 readiness, which matters concretely: FIPS 140-2 certificates move to NIST’s historical list on 22 September 2026, and RHEL 9’s validated OpenSSL, GnuTLS, and kernel crypto modules are the foundation we build on
    • Compliance-driven engineering work, notably the supply-chain security expectations of NIS2 (Article 21(2)(d)) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act — translated into automation and evidence, not spreadsheets

      • You will also contribute to what comes next: threat modelling of the platform, hardening guidance for customers, and security review of significant design changes.


What We Are Looking For

This is a role for someone early in their career who wants to grow into being their team’s security reference. We expect to invest in you, and we expect you to keep growing here for as long as you want to — there is no ceiling built into this seat.

Required

  • Linux is your primary operating system — at work, at home, or both. You are comfortable in the terminal and you reach for a shell before a UI
  • Roughly 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a shorter track record with unusually strong evidence of the skills below
  • Solid working ability in Python and Bash — you will be writing and maintaining real code in a production codebase
  • A genuine, demonstrable interest in security. We care much more about this than about formal credentials. Show it however it is true for you: CTFs, a home lab, reading advisories and CVE writeups for fun, a hardening project, security-adjacent contributions, a blog, anything real
  • Comfortable using Git in a collaborative environment
  • Ability to read and understand existing code before modifying it
  • The judgement to tell a real risk from a scanner’s opinion — and the instinct to check whether vulnerable code is actually reachable before calling it exposed
  • The willingness to say plainly when you are not yet sure, rather than producing an answer you could not defend
  • French — the team works in French day to day
  • Written communication skills in English

    • Nice to Have

    • CVE triage, CVSS scoring, or vulnerability management experience
    • Reading vendor advisories and understanding vendor triage — NVD, RHSA, Red Hat severity and will-not-fix calls
    • Supply-chain security tooling — SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX), scanners (Trivy, Grype, Syft), artifact signing
    • RPM packaging or Linux distribution internals
    • SELinux policy work
    • CI/CD systems, especially GitHub Actions
    • RHEL / Rocky Linux (versions 8 and 9)
    • Containers (Docker, containerd, systemd units)
    • Ansible or Salt
    • Awareness of NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, or FIPS 140-3
    • Familiarity with S3 or object storage concepts
    • Serious use of AI coding tools in a real workflow — Claude Code or equivalent, beyond autocomplete

      • To Be Clear About Scope

      This is a software engineering role with a security mandate. It is not a SOC or incident-response analyst position, not a penetration-testing role, and not a GRC or compliance-documentation role. If what you want is to build the tooling and harden the system yourself, in code, you are in the right place.


What We Offer
  • Dedicated focus. Security is your job here, not the thing you get to after the sprint work is done
  • Clear direction, and a say in it. Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering, and the team is accountable for delivering them. You would not be inventing the agenda on your own, you would help shape what goes on it, and you would be part of making it stick
  • A network of peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams, working the same problems on different perimeters
  • Work that compounds. Customer security questions are a permanent obligation, so every assessment you make reusable and every check you automate keeps paying back, release after release
  • Modern tooling, actually adopted. Claude Code in every engineer’s hands, and a real say in how AI reshapes our build and delivery chain
  • A rare combination: security work with the leverage of owning the whole stack, down to our own Linux distribution
  • Mentorship from senior engineers with deep expertise across Linux, storage, packaging, and distributed systems — you will not be the only person who understands your perimeter
  • A long-term growth path toward becoming your team’s security reference and a senior voice in the network
  • Work that ships to production and runs at exabyte scale, in banking, healthcare, and government
  • Standard French benefits: meal vouchers, Navigo subsidy, mutuelle

title: Scientist II Machine Learning Engineer (LLM & GenAI Specialist)
description: About us Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed. Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity. K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners. Position is based in our Paris offices or remotely in France, UK, or Germany. Please submit your CV in English About the role: We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Scientist II Machine Learning Engineer to design, develop, and deploy cutting-edge AI solutions. In this role, you will focus heavily on Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, and Advanced Deep Learning architectures. You will bridge the gap between experimental data science and production-ready ML systems. Working closely with our Data Science and Engineering teams, you will scale complex models, optimize training and inference pipelines, and leverage cloud ecosystems to deliver robust biomedical solutions. Experience handling health, clinical, or omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, etc.) is a major plus. In particular, you will: Develop scalable machine learning libraries, tooling, and research workflows in close partnership with research and data scientists. Shape research infrastructure requirements and drive tool and software choices in collaboration with the platform team. Champion software engineering best practices across the team, enabling researchers and scientists to write maintainable, testable, efficient, and scalable code. Design and enhance systems for experiment tracking, reproducibility, and end-to-end model lifecycle management. Contribute to and accelerate the rapid prototyping of novel models, helping bridge early research and robust implementation. Other Ad-hoc responsibilities, tasks and projects assigned by the management. About you Required qualifications / experience: Education: Master’s or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related quantitative field with a strong focus on ML/AI. Experience: 5+ years of professional experience in software development with Python and a proven track record of deploying deep learning models into production. ML/DL Frameworks & Ecosystems: Deep understanding of machine learning algorithms, statistical methods, and deep learning frameworks. Mastery of PyTorch or TensorFlow. LLM Specialization: Deep understanding of Transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, and the latest breakthroughs in Generative AI. Extensive experience with Hugging Face, with knowledge in agentic workflows and RAG. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. &nbsp;</p></div><p><strong>Location:</strong> Manufacturing Site (Geneva), Hybrid<br><strong>Travel:</strong> 40% domestic and international.<strong><br>Job ID:</strong> 1921&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>The Role:&nbsp;<br></strong></p> <p>We are looking for a Multi-Site Supply Chain Manager and MRP/ERP Specialist to join our IonQ Quantum Networking &amp; Security Operations Team. Working as a core member of the division production leadership team, you will lead a team of planner and warehouse specialists driving standardization and best practices. You will collaborate closely with Manufacturing Managers, Sales, Procurement, and Finance. lead UAT (user acceptance testing) for planning-related system changes.</li> </ul> <p>Finance Reporting</p> <ul> <li>Prepare and deliver a monthly production and delivery forecast to Finance to support anticipation of next month's revenues.</li> <li>Partner with Finance on monthly sales forecasts (revenue and volume implications), budget and variance analysis (actual vs. forecast/budget) at division level.&nbsp;</li> <li>Plan and coordinate the annual physical inventory count at each site ensuring accuracy and working with Finance to reconcile results against ERP records.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Requirements:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in industrial engineering, Supply Chain Management, or related field required;</li> <li>8+ years of progressive supply chain experience focused on demand/supply planning in a manufacturing environment. We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>US Technical Jobs.&nbsp;</strong>The position you are applying for will require access to technology that is subject to U.S. export control and government contract restrictions.&nbsp; Employment with IonQ is contingent on either verifying “U.S. Person” (e.g., U.S. citizen, U.S. national, U.S. permanent resident, or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum) status for export controls and government contracts work, obtaining any necessary license, and/or confirming the availability of a license exception under U.S. export controls.&nbsp; Please note that in the absence of confirming you are a U.S. Person for export control and government contracts work purposes, IonQ may choose not to apply for a license or decline to use a license exception (if available) for you to access export-controlled technology that may require authorization, and similarly, you may not qualify for government contracts work that requires U.S. Persons, and IonQ may decline to proceed with your application on those bases alone.&nbsp; Accordingly, we will have some additional questions regarding your immigration status that will be used for export control and compliance purposes, and the answers will be reviewed by compliance personnel to ensure compliance with federal law.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>US Non-Technical Jobs.&nbsp;</strong>Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, DeepJudge helps legal teams unlock and apply the knowledge inside their organizations through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure – enabling them to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn institutional knowledge into a lasting advantage.

Every organization can license the same AI models, but no two organizations share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often fragmented across systems, underused, and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available and actionable – helping legal teams find the right information faster, surface relevant knowledge, and apply it where it matters most.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms and legal teams, including Holland & Knight, Gunderson Dettmer, Cozen O’Connor, ArentFox Schiff, CMS Switzerland, Schoenherr, and others.

Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America and Europe, DeepJudge is shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move with urgency, think rigorously, and work closely with our clients to build products that solve meaningful problems. If you want to help define how AI transforms professional knowledge work, we’d love to hear from you.

About the role:

We’re looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to strengthen the systems that power our go-to-market teams.

This is a builder role for someone who can design, implement, and own the processes, workflows, automations, and data architecture that accelerate how we find, engage, win, onboard, retain, and expand customers at scale. You will partner across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Partnership to turn fragmented systems and manual work into a high-leverage GTM engine.

If you naturally think: “This should be an automated system, not a spreadsheet.” …you’ll likely be a strong fit. We would love to connect with you about enabling our rapidly growing revenue team. You will play a key role in increasing internal efficiency and productivity to support the team in creating the best customer experience, and in driving commercial success.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • CRM and revenue tech stack architecture

    • Own end-to-end CRM administration as the single source of truth for revenue activities

    • Manage the design, configuration, and roadmap of a connected revenue tech stack

    • Set and enforce data governance standards: field hygiene, deduplication, permissions, and ongoing data-quality monitoring

  • Automation and data foundation

    • Automate and enrich the manual layer with workflows and LLMs

    • Build and maintain operational dashboards (recurring KPIs, data hygiene, system adoption)

    • Advise with thought leadership on which tooling we procure next as we scale

  • Cross-functional partnership and enablement

  • Critical revenue systems are connected, key workflows are AI-assisted or fully automated

  • Leadership has a real-time view into pipeline, conversion, execution, and customer health

  • Proven track record building revenue systems, processes, and data flows from scratch

  • Persistent problem-solver at your core

  • Sharp entrepreneurial instincts and analytical mindset

  • Excellent cross-functional stakeholder management

What you can look forward to:

  • Helping shape how a category-defining AI company builds and scales its go-to-market engine from the ground up

  • A competitive compensation and equity package that reflects the leverage and strategic importance of the role

At DeepJudge, we believe great teams are built on diverse perspectives and experiences. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Senior Dynamics 365 & Power Platform Technical Lead
description: Your Impact We are looking for a senior, hands-on Dynamics 365 & Power Platform Technical Lead to own the technical development, integration, and lifecycle management of our Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform environment. The role covers Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Dynamics 365 Marketing, together with Microsoft Dataverse, Power Apps, Power Automate, platform integrations, and related Azure services. You will translate business requirements into robust technical solutions and determine when to use standard platform capabilities, configuration, low-code development, or custom code. The role combines hands-on platform development with technical leadership, solution governance, and long-term ownership. This is primarily a Dynamics 365 and Power Platform role . Strong professional software development experience with C#/.NET, React, and TypeScript is a valuable asset where requirements justify custom extensions, components, services, or integrations. You will work closely with business process owners across customer-facing teams, Technical Customer Support, Marketing, Data Engineering, and Corporate IT. Your Contribution: Own the platform : Set the technical direction for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, including architecture, environments, standards, and lifecycle management. Deliver solutions : Design, configure, develop, test, deploy, and maintain solutions across Dynamics 365, Dataverse, Power Apps, and Power Automate. Extend where needed : Develop Dataverse plug-ins, custom APIs, business logic, client-side extensions, and Power Apps Component Framework components when standard or low-code capabilities are insufficient. Integrate enterprise systems : Design and maintain secure, reliable integrations between Dynamics 365, ERP, Microsoft 365, Azure, and other business systems. Ensure engineering quality : Establish appropriate practices for source control, testing, CI/CD, deployment, monitoring, documentation, security, and technical debt management. Lead technical delivery : Translate business requirements into sound solution designs, guide implementation partners, resolve complex technical issues, and ensure delivered solutions meet agreed standards. Role Boundaries and Collaboration The Senior Dynamics 365 & Power Platform Technical Lead is accountable for : Technical architecture and solution design across Dynamics 365 and Power Platform. Dataverse application models, business logic, security configuration, and extensions. Platform integrations, environments, releases, and application lifecycle management. Technical standards, solution quality, and coordination of technical delivery. Business process owners are accountable for : Business processes, priorities, and functional requirements. Business policies and decision-making. User adoption and expected business outcomes. Acceptance of process and solution changes. Data Engineering is accountable for : Microsoft Fabric lakehouses and data pipelines. Analytical data models and governed data products. Power BI platform delivery and analytical reporting. These roles collaborate on data contracts, data quality, lineage, security, and the reliable transfer of Dynamics 365 data into the analytical data platform. Your Background Strong hands-on experience developing and maintaining Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform solutions, ideally including Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service. Strong knowledge of Microsoft Dataverse, including data models, security roles, business logic, solutions, environments, and model-driven applications. Practical experience with Power Apps and Power Automate beyond basic configuration or citizen-development scenarios. Experience extending Dynamics 365 and Dataverse using C# plug-ins, custom APIs, and JavaScript/TypeScript client-side extensions. Experience with REST/OData, the Dataverse Web API, authentication, error handling, and enterprise integration patterns. Practical experience with Power Platform ALM, Git-based source control, CI/CD, testing, and controlled deployment across environments. Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract review. Today we build a holistic platform that changes how legal teams operate from review to negotiation, powered by our Legal Agent. We are looking for the person who makes that value real for customers: in the demo, in onboarding, and inside the AI itself.

When you join Legartis, you don't just take a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and legal experts. We don't chase hype; we build substance.


Your mission

This is not a classic legal role, and not a classic sales or product role. You operate at the intersection of Law, Revenue, and AI, where you are a lever, not a bottleneck: your job is to build the demos, playbooks, and standards that let the whole company scale, and to step into the calls where your expertise closes the gap.

1. Commercial impact. You help win and grow customers. You build and run demos that create a "wow" moment, join high-stakes prospect calls as the legal expert who speaks at eye level with GCs, and run our trials and workshops: onboarding sessions where customers solve their own use cases live, with you coaching. You turn objections into use cases and interest into next steps, and you enable our Sales team to tell the legal story without you in the room. You think of outcomes in terms of trial-to-signature conversion, adoption, expansion.

2. Customer transformation. Once a deal is signed, you make the value real by acting as a strategic sparring partner in onboarding: defining review requirements, tuning playbooks and prompts, and showing legal teams where Legartis delivers the highest ROI. You turn individual learnings into scalable standards and documentation.

3. Making the AI better. You work hands-on with the Legal Agent: prompting, testing, diagnosing where it breaks and why. You feed what you learn from customers back into Product and Engineering (playbook quality, test sets, edge cases) so the product improves with every customer.

4. Internal legal support. You don't just sell the tool; you use it. When necessary, you support Legartis as in-house counsel on contract reviews and specific legal questions.


Your profile

We are honest: people who combine all of this are rare. We hire for aptitude and attitude, assess hands-on in a case study, and train the rest side by side, in real customer work.

1. You can sell the product (key). Not in the cold-calling sense, but in the way a great expert sells: by making the customer succeed in front of their own team. Concretely, this means you can (or want to learn to):

  • Run a live demo with confidence including customized, high-stakes demos and recover gracefully when something doesn't land: pull out a better prompt, adjust on the spot, turn a skeptical question into a stronger result.
  • Coach the customer hands-on. In trials and hackathons, the customer drives and you navigate: you get them to enter their own real legal questions, create the first "wow" moment themselves, and build the habits (saved prompts, reusable workflows) that make them stay.
  • Turn objections into use cases. When a customer says "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves," you respond with a concrete path: a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative. You're straight about limits, because credibility is what closes.
  • Speak at eye level with GCs and legal teams asking sharp discovery questions, translating their friction points into what the product can do, and framing value in their language (ROI, risk, time saved).
  • Always leave with a next step. Trial licenses, a hackathon, a follow-up workshop, a scoped rollout conversation. You instinctively convert interest into momentum, and you remove friction ("we can make that happen") rather than adding process. Ideally you can point to moments where you influenced a deal, a renewal, or an expansion in any prior role.

2. Legal foundation. Solid legal training and hands-on experience with commercial contracts from in-house, law firm, or legal tech. You understand the "why" behind a clause and can teach that logic to an AI and to a customer. A German 2. Staatsexamen is welcome but not required: we explicitly encourage candidates with qualifications from other jurisdictions or non-traditional paths (e.g. law + IT).

3. Hands-on AI builder. You have spent serious time with LLMs, not as a spectator, but pushing them to their limits. You see prompting and evaluation as a craft and enjoy figuring out where AI systems break and how to fix them.

4. Ownership & communication. You can point to things you built, launched, or drove. You are structured enough to run projects with multiple stakeholders, and precise enough to know that a sharp prompt beats a thousand vague instructions. Excellent German and English; other languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, revenue, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • Leverage, not grind. You build the standards, playbooks, and demos that multiply your expertise across the whole company.
  • We invest in you. Structured training on the Legal Agent, side-by-side customer calls, and a clear growth path — we build the capability the market doesn't have yet.
  • True ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).

If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on</span>&nbsp;<br><span data-contrast="auto"> </span>&nbsp;<br><span data-contrast="auto">In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical &amp; thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;134233117&quot;:true,&quot;134233118&quot;:true,&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559740&quot;:240}">&nbsp;</span></p></div><p>&nbsp;</p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">About BridgeBio Pharma, Inc.&nbsp;</span></h4> <p>BridgeBio is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing, and delivering transformative medicines for patients living with genetic diseases and genetically defined cancers. Since our founding in 2015, we have built a diverse portfolio of more than 20 drug development programs, ranging from early discovery to late-stage clinical trials, across multiple therapeutic areas including precision oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, and renal disease. We have already achieved regulatory approval for three therapies and continue to advance promising science from academia into meaningful treatments for patients worldwide.&nbsp;</p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Who We Are&nbsp;</span></h4> <p>BridgeBio is a global biotechnology company with our Global Headquarters located in San Francisco, USA, and our International HQ located in Zug, Switzerland. Since establishing our European presence in 2021, we’ve been building empowered, high-performing teams across countries — with experienced colleagues who move quickly, take ownership, and are fueling the company’s international growth.&nbsp;</p> <p>At BridgeBio, you’ll find an energetic and collaborative culture where pragmatism meets bold decision-making. We embrace uncertainty with confidence, guided by our commitment to making a meaningful impact for patients. Our people are trusted and empowered, united by urgency, purpose, and the drive to advance science for patients around the world.&nbsp;</p> <p>To learn more about our story and company culture, visit us at <a href="https://bridgebio.com">https://bridgebio.com</a></p> <p><strong><u>What You’ll Do</u></strong></p> <p>You will report to the VP, Head of Market Access, International and work closely with international Market Access, regional brand team, and heads or markets access in BridgeBio clusters as well as with field-based colleagues across multiple geographies, to drive strategic initiatives that support BridgeBio’s mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients globally.</p> <p>Your primary purpose will be to secure timely, sustainable patient access to the company’s products by shaping the value narrative, and leading pricing and reimbursement strategies and execution across multiple international markets. This includes oversight of related dossiers, negotiations, and cost coverage approaches. In this role you ensure alignment of Market Access ambitions with clinical value and global pricing interdependencies.</p> <p>You will also be a core member of the International Market Access team, contributing to global decision-making and ensuring alignment across regions while representing diverse market perspectives.</p> <p>This role requires strong collaboration with cross-functional colleagues and external stakeholders across multiple countries to ensure high-quality execution and impact. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in Market Access processes across several international markets and experience introducing innovative therapies in a global biotech environment. You are eager to make a meaningful contribution in pre-launch and launch phases, particularly within rare diseases and orphan conditions, and bring strong communication skills, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, hands-on environment.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong><u>Responsibilities</u></strong></p> <ul> <li>Represent the payer perspective within cross-functional, cross-regional commercialization teams thereby optimizing pricing and market access of the asset.</li> <li>Closely collaborate with HEOR and clusters' leadership teams, Marketing and Clinical Development counterparts to ensure value and access optimization for the asset.</li> <li>Lead early payer engagement with key HTA/payer bodies (e.g. NICE UK, G-BA Germany) to inform evidence generation strategy, value proposition and reimbursement dossiers development.</li> <li>Interact with internal and external experts in pricing, health economics, patient advocacy, health technology assessment authorities, government policy makers and payers as required to execute Pricing &amp; Reimbursement objectives.</li> <li>Provide hands-on support and train local access teams on negotiation strategy and ensure HTA and reimbursement submissions are aligned to the Global and International strategy.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong><u>Where You’ll Work&nbsp; </u></strong></p> <p>This is an office role based and requires in-office collaboration 2-3x per week in our Zug Office.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong><u>&nbsp;</u></strong><strong><u>Who You Are</u></strong></p> <ul> <li>Extensive experience leading HTA submissions and pricing negotiations across multiple international markets, ideally including Europe and other global regions, particularly in rare diseases and orphan conditions.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of international healthcare systems, pricing and reimbursement frameworks, and regulatory environments.</li> <li>Experience generating and leveraging data for HTA submissions and pricing negotiations, with a strong external network of agencies and stakeholders.</li> <li>Comfortable presenting at senior levels and engaging with external thought leaders globally.</li> <li>Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional and multicultural teams (including external partners).</li> <li>Knowledge of product commercialization processes with a hands-on, solution-oriented mindset for building scalable processes and documentation.</li> </ul> <p><strong><u>Rewarding Those Who Make the Mission Possible</u></strong></p> <p>We have high expectations for our team members. Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 300+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, annual revenue now exceeds $100m USD and millions use our browser on on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, our search engine, and the DuckDuckGo subscription. We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including Duck.ai, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place. Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!

Your Team and Role

Working on the Data Science Functional Team, you'll drive product and business impact through statistical modeling, experiment design, Bayesian marketing analysis, and classifier implementation across our search engine, instant answers, AI, and revenue optimization, and work on related projects. Recent projects include:

  • Defining core growth metrics for our products and building the infrastructure to monitor trends and anomalies

  • Measuring the impact of major marketing campaigns for Duck.ai, translating full-funnel data into actionable decisions

  • Building monitoring pipelines to detect unexpected shifts in search traffic patterns faster and more reliably

  • Expanding evaluation datasets for page context understanding across complex scenarios like multi-tab browsing and content reattachment

  • Improving the trigger systems that determine when AI-assisted answers surface in DuckDuckGo Search, balancing quality and our privacy-first approach

 

Our data meets rigorous privacy standards and is necessarily sparse, so you'll need to think creatively to surface actionable insights in an evidence-first culture where quantitative rigor is the baseline, not the exception.

  • You have 7+ years of experience in Data Science and a track record of leading high-complexity projects from scoping to production with minimal direction.

  • Deploy and iterate on ML in production environments

  • Develop and deploy NLP solutions

  • You have advanced SQL and query optimization skills, familiarity with columnar databases like BigQuery, Clickhouse, Redshift, or Druid; experience with a BI tool like Tableau or PowerBI is a plus.

  • You can design, implement, and analyze experiments across product surfaces, and are comfortable deriving insights from sparse or privacy-constrained data.

  • You collaborate effectively with product teams and contribute to overall team throughput.

Deine Rolle Du möchtest einen Markt nicht nur betreuen, sondern aktiv entwickeln und nachhaltige Partnerschaften aufbauen? Du verstehst Vertrieb als Beziehungsgeschäft mit Sinn – besonders im Gesundheitsumfeld? FormMed steht für hochwertige Mikronährstofflösungen, wissenschaftliche Qualität und das gemeinsame Ziel, Gesundheit nachhaltig zu verbessern. In einem respektvollen, lernbereiten Umfeld arbeiten wir täglich daran, medizinische Expertise zugänglich zu machen und echte Wirkung zu erzielen. Als Senior Regional Account Manager Westschweiz (m/w/d) verantwortest du den strategischen und nachhaltigen Ausbau unseres Vertriebsgebiets in der Westschweiz mit den Regionen Genf, Jura, Freiburg, Bern und Wallis. Du entwickelst bestehende Kundenbeziehungen gezielt weiter, identifizierst neue Marktpotenziale und gewinnst neue Partner im Gesundheitswesen. Du repräsentierst FormMed als kompetenten und verlässlichen Partner gegenüber Ärzt, Therapeut, Apotheken und weiteren Gesundheitsfachpersonen. Dabei verbindest du ausgeprägte Vertriebsstärke mit Beratungskompetenz und einem echten Verständnis für die individuellen Bedürfnisse deiner Kunden. Du erhältst viel Gestaltungsspielraum, arbeitest eigenverantwortlich und hast die Möglichkeit, den Schweizer Markt aktiv mitzugestalten. Dabei wirst du Teil eines Teams, das Zusammenarbeit, Vertrauen und kontinuierliche Entwicklung lebt. Wegen unseres stetigen und schnellen Wachstums suchen wir viele neue Kollegen:innen, die uns noch weiter voranbringen und gut ins Team passen. Wachse mit uns und profitiere von einem Umfeld, das Dir große Sicherheit und viele Chancen bietet.

Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll work on the software that runs on our legged security robots: how they perceive their surroundings, know where they are, and move through real customer sites on patrol. You'll join the team that owns everything on the robot and take a well-scoped problem from first experiment to a result that runs on hardware. The role focuses on building software for the robot autonomy stack that runs in the field. We'll agree your focus area with you during the interview process, based on your strengths and the team's priorities, and we expect you to own it from day one. This role is hands-on. You'll work with real sensor data and field logs, test on physical robots, and see first-hand why a robot that works in the lab can still fail on a live site at night, in rain, or after the layout changes. What You'll Work On Build and improve components of the on-robot autonomy stack, such as perception, localisation and state estimation, or planning and navigation, depending on your background and the team's priorities. Integrate sensors such as lidar, cameras and IMU, and work with the data they produce in day, night and challenging weather. Reproduce issues from field deployments using logs and simulation, find the root cause, and help fix it at the right layer. Design repeatable tests and clear metrics that show whether a change holds up across routes, lighting, weather and site layouts. Test your work on physical robots, and join site visits to see how the system behaves in real operating conditions.
